Jin: Heads-up: hitting a messy TS + bundler + edge mismatch while porting the JS SDK sample to Cloudflare. Compiler errors about generics and an overload mismatch, plus a runtime 'is not a function' on some client methods.
Priya: can you paste the exact compiler output? bundlers often change how types are resolved when exports use conditionals.
Jin: key errors: 'TS2345: Argument of type "unknown" is not assignable to parameter of type "T"' and 'No overload matches this call to client.invoke(...)'. Runtime: client.runTool is undefined.
Marco: likely export interop. Our package.json has conditional exports: ./dist/cjs -> cjs entry, ./dist/esm -> esm entry, and types point to ./dist/index.d.ts. Some bundlers resolve to the CJS file even for ESM projects which breaks default vs named import semantics.
Rae: also note edge runtimes don't support Node streams exactly; our retry layer expects node-specific error shapes and uses AbortController slightly differently. That can surface as mysterious failures.
Jin: current tsconfig for the sample: { "target":"es2022", "module":"esnext", "moduleResolution":"bundler", "strict":true, "noImplicitAny":true }. I tried node16/next for moduleResolution and that changed errors but didn't fully fix.
Priya: quick local workaround: set "skipLibCheck": true so type resolution doesn't fail across our .d.ts gaps. Not ideal for CI.
Marco: we should produce a dedicated types entry for edge consumers, e.g., types/edge/index.d.ts, and make sure conditional exports include a "types" path so bundlers pick it up.
Rae: for runtime, I'll add safe guards in retry wrapper: detect if fetch supports signal, fallback to our polyfilled AbortController, and avoid calling request.destroy() which doesn't exist in edge.
Jin: changing imports to named form fixed the runtime missing-method: `import { Client } from '@redwood/inference'` instead of default import. But still TS generic inference is weird when calling client.chat<{ x: number }>(...)
Priya: generics can be lost if the method signatures are declared with overloads that rely on exported type aliases that bundlers drop. Maybe simplify overloads and prefer a single generic method `chat<T = any>(...)` with helper types for stricter layers.
Marco: alternative: keep ergonomic overloads for JS users and ship an opt-in strict typings package for TS power-users. e.g., add a `@redwood/inference/strict` types entry or `types/strict.d.ts` import path.
Rae: we should also add example tsconfigs for each target environment in the repo: tsconfig.node.json, tsconfig.edge.json, tsconfig.strict.json with notes on moduleResolution and lib arrays.
infra-bot: buildkite job #4812 failed for examples/edge-sdk (types) - https://ci.internal/4812
Jin: action items:
- Marco: audit conditional exports and create a stable types path for edge bundlers, update package.json exports (owner: Marco)
- Rae: harden retry/auth wrapper for environments without Node streams and document differences (owner: Rae)
- Priya: propose typings strategy: ergonomic default types + optional strict types entry; sketch PR (owner: Priya)
- Jin: add a minimal repro under examples/edge-ts and publish recommended tsconfig and import style (owner: Jin)
Marco: I'll also add a small test that builds examples with esbuild, rollup, and webpack to catch resolver differences.
Priya: will write a short doc in the repo explaining unknown vs any tradeoffs and how to opt-in to strictness.
Jin: thanks. I'll post the repro link here once pushed. please ping #devex if you run into this while testing samples.
